rows.why: We expect about 11.9 carries vs the 12.5 line. We give the under 61% (needs 56% per pick on Underdog); recent games and the matchup both point lower
rows.why_long: Underdog lower 12.5 needs 56% per pick for your entry; fair view 62% (draftkings 11.5, moved to this line). Averaging 11.2 over the last 8 games, lower than 12.5 in 47% of them (raw 66%, shrunk 62%). Projects 11.9 (raw 56%, shrunk 61%).
why_points: The pick: Carries lower 12.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (draftkings 11.5, moved to this line) is 62%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 11.5. This is the best number for the lower side.
Game log, most recent first: 16, 6, 8, 15, 15, 14, 2, 10. Weighted average 11.2; went lower than 12.5 in 4 of 8 games (47% recency-weighted).
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±4.7, so the line is 0.3 of those swings above his average (standard deviations) — a modest gap.
Projection: we expect 11.9 carries on average; in a typical game 11.5 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 1.0 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 66% and the matchup 56%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 62%, matchup 61%.
Bottom line: we give it 61% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +5.2 points; that works out to about +9¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
rows.glance_head: The under looks good: we expect about 11.5 in a typical game vs the 12.5 line, and his recent games and the matchup agree.
